title: HyMAGE: Semantic-Aware Dynamic Hypergraph Generation

problem.claim: Understanding hypergraph evolution is needed to reveal high-order interaction patterns and generate credible synthetic data when real interaction records are scarce.

gap.claim: Existing models rely on global topological heuristics that treat nodes as passive entities and ignore node attributes' influence on structural evolution, resulting in poor semantic consistency and generalization.

contributions.claim: HyMAGE is a semantic-aware dynamic hypergraph generation framework based on semantic preferential attachment, without graph-structure pretraining or a centralized optimization objective.
HyMAGE models each node as an autonomous agent and uses LLMs for local semantic selection, allowing hyperedge formation and dissolution to emerge from local semantic affinity and structural context.
HyMAGE provides topology-and-semantics-aligned attributed hypergraphs as synthetic training data for downstream hypergraph learning and mining.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show HyMAGE significantly outperforms existing methods at structural and semantic levels.

The authors report that HyMAGE reproduces nine high-order structural patterns of real hypergraphs and supports downstream task generalization, with hypergraph neural networks trained solely on generated data achieving high accuracy and diffusion behaviors closely matching those of real hypergraphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hypergraph evolution is important for understanding high-order interactions and generating synthetic data under data scarcity.
Existing approaches have semantic-consistency, generalization, and node-attribute limitations.
HyMAGE uses semantic preferential attachment, autonomous nodes, and LLM-based local semantic selection without graph-structure pretraining or centralized optimization.
The framework is positioned as both an explanatory generative model and a scalable synthetic data factory for attributed hypergraphs.
Reported experiments indicate structural and semantic performance gains, reproduction of nine structural patterns, and downstream generalization.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses local semantic affinity and structural context to generate hyperedge formation and dissolution.

interpretation.claim: Local agent-level semantic decisions may provide a mechanism for aligning generated structure with node meaning.

application.claim: For attributed relational synthesis, consider combining local semantic selection with structural context rather than relying only on global topology.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when local semantic selection may fail or how its costs and errors are controlled.

source_observation.claim: HyMAGE-generated data reportedly supports accurate downstream hypergraph neural network training and diffusion behavior close to that of real hypergraphs.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic data quality may be assessed through both downstream task performance and behavioral similarity to real relational systems.

application.claim: Evaluate synthetic relational data with task-based and process- or diffusion-based criteria.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings needed to assess the reported comparisons.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the LLMs, prompting, computational requirements, or scalability limits.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
